implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control Policy (2024) was revised and approved 2026-09-17, effective 2026-10-01 (P06). The authenticator and privileged access standard (STD-06) exists; the procedure for manufacturer portal and contact center accounts is due 2026-12-31.

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); Ticketing and POS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Named accounts are created in the identity provider from the HR system feed and federated to SYS-01, the cloud accounts, and the SIEM. Terminations disable identity provider access automatically. SYS-01 access is reviewed quarterly. Gaps: manufacturer portal (SYS-08) and contact center (SYS-12) accounts are created by hand, are not disabled from the HR feed, and have never been reviewed; P07 found 9 of 25 sampled leavers still active in a manufacturer portal.
evidence: HR feed configuration; IdP export; SYS-01 quarterly review records (2025-Q3 to 2026-Q2); P07 samples

implementation_statement: Account creation and disablement are automated from the HR feed for the identity provider and every federated application. SYS-08 and SYS-12 do not support federation today, so their accounts are manual (gap 7).

SYS-01 enforces 9 roles (advisor, store technician, Depot technician, data recovery, Store Manager, partner desk, finance, administrator, read-only audit). The restricted passcode field is visible only to the assigned technician and is purged at release. Gaps: about 11,800 legacy tickets still hold passcodes in notes readable by every role (gap 2); delivery links for business accounts never expire (gap 3).
evidence: SYS-01 role matrix; field permission settings; P03 search 2026-07-15

implementation_statement: SD-WAN policies separate store traffic, guest Wi-Fi, payment terminals, and the corporate network. At 22 stores and the Depot, bench PCs and customer devices sit on their own VLAN with no route to counter, office, or lab networks. The 12 older stores are flat (gap 6).
evidence: SD-WAN policy export; P07 reachability test

implementation_statement: Developers cannot deploy to production without a second approver; SYS-01 refunds above $250 need a Store Manager; backup administrators are separate from workload administrators.
evidence: Pipeline approval settings; SYS-01 refund rule; backup role list

implementation_statement: The customer data access standard (2025) limits technician access to device content to the repair test checklist. Office users have no local administrator rights. Gaps: session recording and USB blocking cover only the standard bench image (Depot and 20 stores); the 48 legacy-image bench PCs at 14 stores allow USB storage and keep no session record (gap 1).
evidence: Customer data access standard; bench image settings; P07 test at 3 stores
regulatory_driver: N81-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(n)); N81-R02 (Fla. Stat. 501.171(2)); Manufacturer A agreement (contract)

implementation_statement: Administrators use separate privileged accounts for the identity provider, cloud, and SYS-01 administration. Gap: 4 Depot supervisors use their everyday accounts for SYS-01 administrator functions.
evidence: IdP privileged group export; SYS-01 administrator list

implementation_statement: Privileged roles are limited to 11 named people (identity, cloud, SYS-01, SIEM) and elevated just in time in the cloud accounts.
evidence: Privileged account list; just-in-time elevation logs

implementation_statement: The identity provider locks accounts after 10 failed attempts and applies risk-based sign-in checks.
Office endpoints lock after 10 minutes idle; counter tablets lock after 2 minutes and require badge plus PIN; bench PCs lock after 10 minutes.
SYS-01 sessions end after 30 minutes idle and at the end of each counter session.

Remote access for staff uses the identity provider with MFA and device compliance checks. Gap: the lab storage vendor and the SYS-01 vendor support team use their own remote tools when invited; sessions are not recorded and are approved by email.
evidence: Conditional access policy; vendor support tickets

implementation_statement: Store Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication for staff devices; guest Wi-Fi is isolated from all company networks and payment terminals.
Counter tablets and company phones are enrolled in device management with remote wipe. Personal phones may reach email only through the protected mobile app.
POL-05 prohibits copying customer data to personal devices or personal cloud storage. Gap: technicians on legacy bench images could connect personal phones (the March 2026 Store 17 case).
POL-05 and the training standard set annual and role-based training requirements (P06).

Annual security awareness training (96% completion) and quarterly phishing simulations (June 2026 click rate 6.9%). Gap: contact center agents and store advisors get no training on payment terminal tampering or on card numbers in calls.

Insider threat awareness is part of technician onboarding since 2025 and covers what counts as snooping and how to report it. Gap: no annual refresher; Store Managers are not trained to spot warning signs.
Role-based training exists for administrators and developers (secure coding course, 2025). Gap: data recovery specialists and the partner claims desk have no role-based security training.
The logging and monitoring standard (STD-02) is in draft; POL-03 sets the logging requirements.

The identity provider, EDR, firewalls, SD-WAN, and cloud audit logs go to the SIEM. Gaps: SYS-01 audit events (exports and bulk views), the lab storage array, and the mail-in portal application logs are not collected (gap 8).
Collected logs include user, time, source, action, and outcome; time is synchronized from the cloud and SD-WAN time sources.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews alerts 24x7 and escalates high-severity alerts within 30 minutes. Gap: nobody reviews SYS-01 export or bulk-view activity, so the March 2026 snooping case and any bulk export would not be detected from logs.
Cloud audit logs and SIEM archives are written to a locked log bucket in the shared services account that workload administrators cannot change.
SIEM data is searchable for 1 year and archived for 3 years. Gap: SYS-01 keeps audit events for only 90 days and they are not exported.
evidence: SIEM retention setting; SYS-01 audit settings

implementation_statement: Audit generation is enabled on the identity provider, cloud, EDR, and network devices. Gap: bench session recording runs only on the standard bench image.
The co-sourced internal audit firm assesses selected controls each year (P07, 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-21).

Interconnections with Partners P1 and P2 use the partner integration API with mutual TLS and are covered by the partner agreements. Gap: the agreements have no technical interconnection schedule (data elements, keys, contacts, outage notice).
The POA&M is kept by the GRC Analyst and reviewed monthly by the IT Director and quarterly by the audit committee.
The Chief Operating Officer accepted operation of the STPP with conditions on 2026-09-17 (SSP section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring covers EDR, identity, cloud posture, and quarterly scans. Gap: metrics for retention, sanitization, and PIN pad inspections are not monitored centrally.

Tailored in (not in the Moderate baseline) because the company builds internet-facing software. An external penetration test of the mail-in portal and partner API runs every year (last 2026-05; 1 High finding fixed 2026-06-10). Gap: no test of the store network or bench image.
POL-01 and POL-04 set configuration requirements. The configuration standard (STD-01) is in draft.

Baselines exist for office endpoints, counter tablets, the standard bench image, and cloud guardrails. Gaps: the legacy bench image (48 PCs) has no documented baseline; container images have no hardening baseline.

Application changes to the mail-in portal and partner API go through pull requests with one peer reviewer and a separate approver for production. Gap: infrastructure and SD-WAN changes are approved by email without a change record.

Cloud guardrails block public storage and unencrypted volumes. Gaps: no benchmark-based settings for bench images or container hosts; P07 found vendor default administrator passwords on CCTV recorders at 5 of 8 visited stores.
Application allowlisting runs on counter tablets. Bench PCs on the standard image block unapproved software and USB storage. Gap: legacy bench PCs allow any software and USB storage.
evidence: Device management profiles; bench image settings

implementation_statement: Endpoint and cloud inventories are generated from device management and the cloud asset service. Gaps: the payment terminal list differs from the processor list by 6 devices; 9 bench PCs found in P07 were not in the inventory.
Software is licensed through IT; manufacturer diagnostic tools are installed only from the manufacturer portals.
Users cannot install software on office endpoints or counter tablets. Gap: legacy bench PCs allow technician-installed tools.
POL-03 covers contingency; the contingency and recovery standard (STD-07) is due 2026-12-31.

No written contingency plan exists beyond the 2024 ransomware plan. A plan built on this BIA (P05), with store downtime kits, a manual claims desk, and Depot relocation steps, is due 2027-01-31 (POAM-007).
Contingency training for Store Managers, the claims desk, and the lab will start when the plan is approved (2027-Q1).

Only one restore test has run (a file restore from the workloads account in 2025). Full restore of the lab storage and a recovery test of the mail-in portal and partner API are scheduled from 2026-11-16 (POAM-007).
Backups are stored in the separate backup account in a second region with 30-day write-once retention and separate administrator credentials.
Stores can take intake for each other within a region. Gap: no alternate site for the Depot functions (mail-in receiving, partner repairs, data recovery).
Every store has cellular failover on the SD-WAN edge; the Depot and corporate office have dual ISPs.

Cloud workloads are backed up daily to the backup account; the lab storage is backed up nightly; SYS-01 is exported weekly (encrypted) to the backup account. Gap: the lab backup includes about 27 TB of data past retention (gap 3).
evidence: Backup job reports (July 2026: 31 of 31 days successful)

implementation_statement: Recovery runbooks for the mail-in portal and partner API (rebuild from images and infrastructure code) are planned with the CP-4 tests.
POL-02 and STD-06 set identification and authentication rules.

Every workforce member has a unique identity in the identity provider. Counter tablets use badge plus PIN for named sessions. Exception: manufacturer portals and the contact center platform use local named accounts (gap 7).
MFA (push with number matching) is enforced for all privileged accounts through conditional access.
evidence: Conditional access policy; P07 test (25 of 25)

implementation_statement: MFA is enforced for all named users of federated applications. Gap: contact center and manufacturer portal local accounts rely on the vendors' MFA settings, which are not enforced for 2 of 3 platforms.
Push MFA with number matching and time-limited tokens resists replay.

Passwords are at least 14 characters with a banned list; service credentials for the partner API are in the cloud secrets service. Gaps: pipeline secrets sit in pipeline variables (gap 10); vendor default passwords on CCTV recorders (P07).
Customers use the status portal with a ticket number and a one-time code sent to the phone on file; release requires photo ID or the one-time code. Gap: business account delivery links need no code.
POL-03 Incident Response Policy revised 2026-09-17 (P06).
Incident roles are trained for ransomware only. Store Managers, the partner desk, and the contact center have no incident training.
The last tabletop was in March 2025 (ransomware). Exercises for both P08 runbooks are scheduled for 2026-11-18 and 2027-02-17.
The MSSP contains endpoint threats 24x7. Gaps: no handling procedure for insider snooping, lab data exposure, or checkout skimming; the March 2026 Store 17 case was handled ad hoc (gap 13).
Incidents are tracked in the security incident queue with discovery time, severity, and closure.

Staff report suspected incidents to the service desk security line. Gap: the contract clocks (acquirer 24 hours, Manufacturer A 24 hours, partners 48 hours) are not in the plan or the notification matrix used before this assessment.
regulatory_driver: N81-R02 (Fla. Stat. 501.171(3); (4); (6)); Manufacturer A agreement (contract); Partner agreements (contract)

implementation_statement: The MSSP and the cyber insurer's panel (breach counsel and forensics) provide response support.
The 2024 incident response plan covers ransomware only. Runbooks for device data exposure and point-of-sale compromise were approved 2026-09-17 (P08) and will be exercised.
Vendor maintenance of the lab storage array and SYS-01 support sessions are approved by email; no session recording (see AC-17).
POL-04 sets media and device handling rules. The sanitization standard (STD-04) is being updated to SP 800-88 Rev. 2.
Customer devices awaiting repair or pickup are kept in locked cabinets; lab drives are kept in the lab safe.
Mail-in devices ship with tracking and signature; recovered data on drives is shipped encrypted. Gap: the courier contract has no loss-handling or data terms.

The Depot sanitizes recycling devices and retired media with per-device certificates under an SP 800-88 Rev. 1 procedure. Gaps: 12 of 34 stores wipe drop-off devices with no certificate; no validation step as described in SP 800-88 Rev. 2 section 4.5.2; recycler certificates list lots only (gap 4).
evidence: Depot certificates; store logs; recycler certificates

implementation_statement: USB storage is blocked on office endpoints and standard bench images; data transfer for customers uses approved encrypted transfer drives logged per ticket. Gap: legacy bench PCs allow any USB storage.
evidence: Device control policy; transfer drive log

implementation_statement: The facility security standard (STD-10) covers stores, the Depot, and the lab.
Badge access controls the Depot, the lab, and corporate IT rooms; store back rooms use keys. Gap: store key logs are not kept at 6 of 8 visited stores.
CCTV covers counters, benches, and the lab door with 30-day retention. Gap: CCTV recorders at 5 of 8 visited stores used vendor default passwords (P07).
Policies POL-01 to POL-05 were revised and approved 2026-09-17.
This SSP, approved 2026-09-17.
Every workforce member acknowledges POL-05 at hire (98% for 2026). Gap: annual re-acknowledgment not collected for store staff.
Tailored in. The IT Director is the designated Information Security Officer in writing; the vCISO sets strategy and reports to the audit committee.
Tailored in. The risk management strategy and risk appetite were approved by the Chief Executive Officer on 2026-09-17 (P01).
POL-01 and HR procedures cover screening, termination, transfer, and sanctions.
Background checks are completed before hire for all technicians, data recovery specialists, field technicians, and contact center agents.

HR records terminations; identity provider access is disabled automatically. Gaps: local manufacturer portal and contact center accounts are removed by email request, late in 9 of 25 sampled cases; badge return is not tracked at stores.
Transfers update identity provider groups automatically. Gap: SYS-01 store assignments are not updated when technicians move stores.
All technicians, data recovery specialists, and agents sign the customer data confidentiality agreement at hire (since 2025) and at the 2025 rollout for existing staff.
Agency temporary staff at the Depot during peak season sign the confidentiality agreement. Gap: the overflow answering service contract has no confidentiality or card data terms.
POL-01 4.8 sets sanctions; misuse of customer device data is grounds for termination (applied in the March 2026 Store 17 case).
POL-01 sets the risk assessment method (SP 800-30 Rev. 1).
Information types are categorized in this SSP (section 6) and data classes in POL-04.
An enterprise risk assessment using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 was completed 2026-07-31 and updated with P07 findings (P01, 50 risks).
Supply chain risk is assessed for Tier 1 vendors through SOC 2 reviews (5 done). Gap: the recycler, courier, and AI vendors were never assessed (gap 11).

Quarterly authenticated scans of endpoints and cloud workloads; annual penetration test of the portal and API. Gaps: scans moved to monthly only for internet-facing systems in 2026-06; 7 of 40 sampled Critical findings exceeded the 30-day target.
Risks are tracked to treatment in the register and the POA&M.
Security and data-use terms are in the SYS-01, cloud, identity, MSSP, and payment contracts. Gap: 7 vendors with customer data have no security or data-use terms (gap 11).
The partner API uses mutual TLS, per-partner keys, and object-level authorization checks since the 2026-05 test. Gap: no written secure design principles for the team.
Tier 1 vendors provide SOC 2 Type 2 reports or PCI DSS AOCs, reviewed yearly (P09). Gaps: only 5 of 9 Tier 1 reviews done; complementary user entity controls for SYS-01 are partly unmet.
Developers write unit and integration tests; the annual penetration test covers both applications. Gap: no static analysis, dependency scanning, or secret scanning in the pipeline (gap 10).

31 bench PCs run an unsupported operating system because legacy diagnostic tools need it. Compensating controls today: none beyond the store firewall. Planned: isolate them on an offline bench segment and replace by 2027-06-30.
Site firewalls and cloud firewalls deny inbound traffic by default; the mail-in portal and partner API sit behind a web application firewall. Gap: 12 older stores have flat internal networks (gap 6).
regulatory_driver: N81-R02 (Fla. Stat. 501.171(2)); N81-R03 (PCI DSS v4.0.1 SAQ P2PE eligibility)

control_name: Deny by Default: Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Cloud and Depot networks deny by default. Store networks at the 12 older stores allow any internal traffic.
TLS 1.2 or higher protects the portal, the API (mutual TLS for partners), and SaaS sessions; SD-WAN tunnels are encrypted. P2PE encrypts card data in the terminal.
Encryption keys for cloud storage and databases are managed in the cloud key service with company-managed keys; backup keys are separate.

provider_if_inherited: Payment processor and gateway (PCI DSS AOC)
implementation_statement: Validated algorithms are used by the cloud services and SaaS vendors; the P2PE solution provider manages terminal encryption and keys.

provider_if_inherited: Ticketing and POS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); Cloud provider (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: SYS-01 and cloud storage encrypt data at rest; office endpoints use full-disk encryption. Gap: the lab storage array encrypts only the newer shelf (about 40 TB of the 95 TB used); bench PCs are not encrypted.
Office endpoints and cloud images are patched monthly. Gaps: legacy bench PCs are patched by hand; 7 of 40 sampled Critical findings were late.
EDR runs on all office endpoints and 190 of 238 bench PCs with 24x7 MSSP response. Gap: 48 legacy-image bench PCs have signature antivirus only.
The MSSP monitors EDR, identity, firewall, and cloud signals. Gaps: no monitoring of SYS-01 exports or bulk views; no change or tamper detection on the mail-in checkout page (gap 5).

Container images are signed and verified at deployment; SYS-01 maintains record integrity (vendor SOC 2). Gap: repair outcome messages to partners are not reconciled daily, so missing or duplicate outcomes are found only at invoicing.
The partner API validates message schemas and rejects malformed claims; the portal validates all form fields server-side.

POL-04 sets retention: tickets 3 years after last service; recovered data 30 days after delivery (90 days with consent). Gaps: customer records since 2016 never purged; the lab purge job has failed since 2025-11 (about 27 TB); legacy passcode notes (gap 2 and gap 3).
evidence: Retention schedule; lab storage listing; P03 searches

implementation_statement: Tier 1 suppliers are reviewed yearly through SOC 2 reports and PCI DSS AOCs (P09). Gap: the review program is new (5 reviews completed in 2026).
